subject: Re: Renewal — locking pricing with multi-year prepay options
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@finedge.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Gomez <alyssa.gomez@finedge.com>
Date: 2026-02-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal pricing — looking to lock rate

Hi Vivek,

We’re starting renewal planning and want to avoid sticker shock next year. Would Redwood do a multi-year prepay to lock pricing for us?

High level: current run-rate usage roughly $620k ARR, expected growth to ~1.1M ARR over 12 months if trends hold. We prefer a structure that gives us price protection but leaves room to scale — open to 3-year prepay or annual prepay with stepped commitments.

Can you share the options and what level of discount you can offer for 1yr vs 3yr prepay? Also interested in ramp examples (Year 1 / Year 2 / Year 3 split).

Thanks — Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of Platform Engineering, FinEdge
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@finedge.com>
Cc: Alyssa Gomez <alyssa.gomez@finedge.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-22T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing — looking to lock rate

Thanks for the note, Daniel — appreciate the heads-up. Below are 3 practical structures we commonly use to provide price certainty while balancing Redwood's capacity and margin constraints. Attaching a term sheet + a sample prepay ramp schedule for clarity.

Options (high level)
- Option A — 1yr annual prepay: prepay 100% for one year. Discount: ~15% off public list for the prepay portion. Fastest to execute; no long-term commitment beyond 12 months.
- Option B — 3yr stepped prepay (recommended for price lock): prepay majority of Year 1, then smaller annual top-ups. Typical split we model: Year1 60% prepay, Year2 25%, Year3 15%. Effective blended discount: ~22% across term (guaranteed price cap).
- Option C — 3yr full upfront: prepay full 3 years up front. Deeper discount: ~30% off list; best unit economics but heavier cash flow requirement.

Key notes / constraints
- Overages: standard overage rate applies to usage above committed units; we can negotiate a lower overage cap (e.g., 50% of list overage) for multi-year prepay but need finance signoff.
- Price protection: we can include a price cap for identical SKU classes; new product SKUs introduced later are out of scope.
- Ramp flexibility: customers may top-up in-year; top-ups convert to prepay dollars at the contracted rate.

Ask from your side
- Confirm target committed ARR and whether the intent is to prepay units or dollar amount (helps structuring).
- Any required billing cadence / PO constraints for procurement?

Next steps
1) If you like Option B, we’ll circulate a term sheet with exact discount and invoice schedule (attached). 2) Finance and legal need to review; Marissa will lead the paperwork.

Attachments: FinEdge_3yr_term_sheet_v2.pdf (term sheet, draft), prepay_ramp_schedule.xlsx (sample ramps)

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-23T08:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing — looking to lock rate

Vivek — quick internal note on concessions and cadence.

Pricing guidance (internal)
- Floor discount levels: 1yr prepay = up to 15% off list; 3yr stepped = up to 22% blended; 3yr upfront = up to 30% (requires exec approval).
- Finance will need modeled cash flow / IRR for 3yr upfront; Sean, can you run a quick sensitivity on effective margin at 30%?
- Overage cap we can offer: up to 50% discount on standard overage fees for stepped prepay; anything deeper requires VP sign-off.

Commercial guardrails for the deal team
- Don’t exceed 25% concession vs. our published enterprise pricing without Mary/VP approval.
- Require a 60–90 day renewal/notice window embedded in the term sheet to avoid immediate churn risk.

I’ll draft suggested term language for the price cap and invoice schedule. Marissa, please prep the HubSpot deal update and the DocuSign template so we can move quickly once the customer confirms.

Aisha Rahman
VP, Sales — Enterprise Accounts
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@finedge.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Gomez <alyssa.gomez@finedge.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T10:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing — looking to lock rate

Thanks Vivek — that framework is helpful. After internal review we prefer a 3-year stepped prepay (Option B) but with a slightly more front-loaded Year 1 to protect against near-term price moves. Proposed structure:
- Year1: 70% prepay of Year1 committed spend
- Year2: 20% prepay (billed at start of Year2)
- Year3: 10% prepay

Requests / asks
- Confirm a firm price-cap clause for the contracted SKUs across the 3-year term (no increases above agreed list for those SKUs).
- Request that overage rate be capped at 1.25x list (instead of default 1.5x) for the term.
- Need PO process: can you accept annual invoices tied to each prepay tranche? DocuSign ready on our side.

We’re comfortable committing to a ~2.5x multiple of baseline compute (approx 1.55M blended ARR over 3 years) if we can get the cap and the overage concession above.

If you can confirm, we’ll route to procurement and sign.

—Daniel
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@finedge.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-28T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal pricing — locking pricing with multi-year prepay options

Daniel — appreciate the counter and the clarity on commitment. We can move forward on the following, subject to final legal and finance signoff:

Agreed commercial summary
- Program: 3-year stepped prepay (finalized ramp): Year1 65% prepay, Year2 20%, Year3 15%. We adjusted Year1 down slightly from your 70% to preserve topping-up flexibility; you may top-up within Year1 at the contracted rate.
- Discount: blended 21.5% across committed dollars (ref in attached term sheet).
- Price protection: price-cap clause for contracted SKU classes for the 36-month term (see §3 in attached term sheet). New product SKUs introduced by Redwood are excluded until expressly added.
- Overage: capped at 1.25x list (as requested) for the term.
- Billing: Redwood can issue annual invoices tied to each prepay tranche. We’ll include invoice milestones in DocuSign.

Next steps to execute
1) Marissa will open the HubSpot deal and attach the final term sheet. (HubSpot link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567)
2) Legal to issue DocuSign (https://www.docusign.com/contract/REDF-FT-2026-0419). Marissa / Sean will coordinate the finance approvals and invoicing schedule.
3) Customer to confirm PO requirements and authorized signers.

Attachments: FinEdge_3yr_term_sheet_v2.pdf, prepay_ramp_schedule.xlsx

If that all looks good, we’ll queue the DocuSign and finance will prep the first invoice for the Year1 tranche. Thanks — excited to keep you at predictable rates.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
